title: Fix volunteer registration and add volunteer markers to ResourceMapPage

requirements.summary: Fix volunteer registration form to persist data, update UI immediately on success, and display clear success/error messages
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting the volunteer registration form calls the backend addVolunteer (or equivalent) mutation with the correct payload.
On success, the new volunteer appears in the volunteer directory list immediately (React Query cache is invalidated/refetched).
A success notification or inline message is shown after a volunteer is successfully added.
If the mutation fails, a visible error message is displayed and the form data is preserved.
The volunteer count on the Dashboard stat card reflects the newly added volunteer.

file_operations.description: Fix the volunteer registration form submission handler to correctly call the useRegisterVolunteer mutation hook with all required fields (name, skills, city, isActive). On success, invalidate the 'volunteers' query key to refresh the list immediately and display a success message using a toast or inline alert. On error, display a clear error message and preserve the form data. Ensure the form includes all fields required by the backend Volunteer interface (id is auto-generated, so exclude it from the form payload).

Review the useRegisterVolunteer mutation hook to ensure it correctly calls actor.registerVolunteer with the Volunteer payload and properly invalidates the 'volunteers' and 'dashboardStats' query keys on success using queryClient.invalidateQueries. Verify error handling returns meaningful error messages to the UI. Confirm the mutation accepts the correct payload shape matching the backend Volunteer interface (excluding auto-generated id).

requirements.summary: Add volunteer markers to ResourceMapPage map, displaying distinct markers with popups showing volunteer details, or a sidebar list if location data is unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: The ResourceMapPage fetches volunteer data from the backend and renders volunteer markers (or a sidebar volunteer list) on/alongside the Leaflet map.
Volunteer markers are visually distinct from hospital markers (different color or icon).
Clicking a volunteer marker opens a popup showing the volunteer's name, city, skills, and availability status.
The sidebar or map includes a section or legend distinguishing hospitals from volunteers.
The map does not break or throw errors if no volunteer location data is available; a graceful fallback (e.g., sidebar list of volunteers) is shown instead.

file_operations.description: Add volunteer markers to the Leaflet map by fetching volunteers using the existing useGetVolunteers hook. For each volunteer with a city field, derive approximate lat/lng coordinates using a best-effort city-to-coordinates mapping (e.g., a lookup table of major cities or use the volunteer's city as a text label). Render volunteer markers using a distinct color/icon (e.g., green or purple vs. the red hospital markers, potentially using the generated volunteer-icon.dim_128x128.png asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/volunteer-icon.dim_128x128.png as a custom Leaflet icon). Each volunteer marker popup should display the volunteer's name, city, skills as badges, and availability status (isActive). If volunteer location data cannot be derived, display volunteers in a dedicated sidebar section listing them by city. Add a legend or section header distinguishing hospitals from volunteers. Ensure graceful error handling if volunteer data is unavailable.
